newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy rejects big power NATO meeting as "useless".
newsitem.headline: Italy rejects big power NATO meeting as "useless".

text.p: Italy, left out of France's plan for a big-powers NATO meeting with Russia, on Thursday dismissed the proposed summit as "useless".
"We do not agree that there should be meetings between a few countries...We don't see the use," Foreign Minister Lamberto Dini told a news conference.

"Security concerns us all, it's not something that can be divided up between countries. We cannot but oppose meetings between a few when in NATO all countries have the same parity in decisions which have to be taken."

Italy has been offended by big-nation initiatives in the past, such as being excluded from the Contact Group on the former Yugoslavia, and is now fighting not to be left out of the hard core of European union states which form a single currency.
France, determined that Washington should not set the agenda for NATO enlargement, is seeking a Big Powers summit in Paris in April ahead of an alliance meeting in July in Madrid.

Paris said earlier that no decision had been taken on the idea, which has been supported by Germany and cautiously backed by Britain but virtually ruled out by the United States. Russia welcomes the proposal as proof its concerns are being taken seriously.
The meeting, which would be attended by the leaders of Russia, the United States, France, Britain and Germany, would be aimed at overcoming Moscow's hostility to NATO enlargement.

Dini earlier told a joint session of the Foreign Affairs and Defence Commissions of the Chamber of Deputies (lower house) that NATO should finalise details of "the special relationship which we must consolidate with Russia" before the July 9 summit.
The Madrid meeting is due to invite former Soviet bloc and central European countries to apply for alliance membership and Dini said Slovenia and Romania should be candidates.

He was cautious on who should run NATO's Southern Command in Naples, Italy. The United States is currently in charge of the strategic base, which controls the Mediterranean region. The issue sparked a row between Paris and Washington last year.

Dini said the objective should be to "preserve the mechanisms which have worked with full efficiency up till now" and said a more European dimension could be achieved by rotating the role of Supreme Vice-Commander in Europe between Europeans.
